## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 91–93 (*Sikkhamānā-sāmaṇerī-gihinī-ummaddāpana*) is a sequence of three disciplinary rules in the Bhikkhunī Vibhaṅga of the Pali Vinaya Piṭaka. The text sets out offenses of expiation (*pācittiya*) incurred by a nun regarding bodily care: a nun who has herself rubbed or massaged by a female trainee (*sikkhamānā*, Pācittiya 91), a novice nun (*sāmaṇerī*, Pācittiya 92), or a laywoman / householder (*gihinī*, Pācittiya 93) must confess the offense. The text has been translated into English by Bhikkhu Brahmali.

 Computational analysis by DharmaNexus shows no cross-language matches scoring 10 or above, but identifies substantial Pali-internal text reuse comprising 299 matching passages across 78 Pali texts [DharmaNexus].
